sections.h2: What does the Winnebago County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Winnebago County Register of Deeds is the official county repository for real estate records, vital records and military discharges. The real estate side holds deeds, land contracts, mortgages, UCC realty filings, plats, certified survey maps and federal tax liens.

When a house in Winnebago County is sold, the deed from the seller to the buyer is recorded here, and the office collects the Wisconsin real estate transfer fee at the same moment. The office phone is 920-232-3390. The county seat is Oshkosh.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Winnebago County?
sections.html:
Recording a deed in Winnebago County costs a flat $30, no matter how many pages the deed has. The county's fee schedule traces the flat fee to Wisconsin Act 314 of 2010, and the statute, Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag), sets the same $30 for recording any document entitled to be recorded.

ItemWinnebago County charge
Recording a deed, mortgage, land contract or satisfaction$30 flat
Copy of a recorded document$2 for the first page, $1 for each added page
Certified copyAdd $1 for the certificate
Subdivision, cemetery or condominium plat$50
Real estate transfer fee$3 per $1,000 of value, rounded up to the next hundred, unless exempt

Source: Winnebago County Register of Deeds fee schedule.

The office takes cash, money orders and personal checks. Debit and credit cards work for in-office orders only, with a $2.50 surcharge on amounts up to $50. Fees are payable in advance by whoever asks for the service, so plan the payment before the deed goes in.

sections.h2: How much is the Wisconsin transfer fee in Winnebago County, and who pays it?
sections.html:
The seller pays a transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value, and the Register of Deeds collects it when the deed is submitted for recording. State law puts the fee on the grantor, who is the seller, and counts any fraction of $100 as a full $100. On a $250,000 sale that works out to 2,500 units of $100 at 30 cents, or $750.

The value is not only the cash the seller receives. Under Wis. Stat. 77.21(3), the value of a sale is the full actual consideration paid or to be paid, including the amount of any lien on the property. For a gift or a deed with nominal consideration, the value is the estimated open-market price. A land contract is measured by the total principal the buyer agrees to pay.

The money is divided by statute: the county keeps 20 percent of what it collects and the rest goes to the state. The register has no duty to check the value or whether an exemption claim is valid, so the seller and buyer answer for what they report.

sections.h2: Which Winnebago County transfers are exempt from the transfer fee?
sections.html:
A transfer is exempt only if it fits a category in Wis. Stat. 77.25, and the reason must be stated on the face of the deed by subsection number. Several categories matter to families and sellers in distress:

  • Transfers between parent and child, stepparent and stepchild, parent and son-in-law or daughter-in-law, or grandparent and grandchild for nominal or no consideration.
  • Transfers between an individual and a domestic partner.
  • Transfers by will, descent or survivorship.
  • A foreclosure, or a deed in lieu of foreclosure, to a mortgage holder or a land contract seller.
  • A sale for delinquent taxes or assessments.
  • A conveyance of real estate with a value of $1,000 or less.

Exemptions are read strictly, and court decisions summarized with the statute show that a move between two entities can be taxed even when the owners are family. If a deed to or from an LLC or trust is involved, read the exemption wording or ask the Register of Deeds before you sign.

sections.h2: How do you file the transfer return for a Winnebago County deed?
sections.html:
You file a Real Estate Transfer Return with the Wisconsin Department of Revenue, and the receipt or exemption number goes with the deed to the Register of Deeds. The return must be signed by both grantor and grantee, and the register may not accept the conveyance for recording without a completed return and the fee.

On January 12, 2026 the Department of Revenue announced that the new return is filed in My Tax Account. The announcement says no registration, username or password is needed to file, and filers can file, view or amend a return. The department's RETR page has user guides, a walk-through video and a list of transfer fee exemptions. Questions go to retr@wisconsin.gov.

Winnebago County's own page for the return says an electronic transfer receipt and the fee, or an exemption number, are required for every conveyance. Some exempt transfers need no return at all under Wis. Stat. 77.255, so ask the register's office if you are unsure which kind of deed you hold.

sections.h2: What must a deed look like to be recorded in Winnebago County?
sections.html:
A deed must meet the state's standard format, or the register may refuse it. Wis. Stat. 59.43(2m) lists the requirements, among them:

  • A clear document name between 0.5 inch and 6 inches from the top of the first page.
  • A blank space of at least 3 inches by 3 inches in the upper right corner of the first page, inside the margins, for recording information.
  • Return information on the first page, except for a document recorded electronically.
  • A parcel identification number for each parcel affected, in a county that requires one.
  • A page 8.5 inches wide and either 11 or 14 inches long, with the pages not hinged or joined along the top or sides.

The county's fee schedule gives 8.5 by 14 inches as the maximum sheet, counts one side of a sheet as a page and treats an attached rider as another page. Title companies and attorneys usually handle this for a sale, but a seller who prepares a quitclaim or a family deed alone should check each item before mailing it.

sections.h2: How does tag-less and electronic recording work in Winnebago County?
sections.html:
Since May 1, 2023 the office has recorded paper documents under a tag-less process: no recording stamp goes on the paper, and the recorded copy comes back electronically. A signed SWIFT Agreement, submitted when you record, gives you access to the official copy. You then receive a link, valid for 7 days, that lets you print up to 3 copies. After 3 copies or 7 days, regular copy fees apply.

The original paper is shredded 30 days after recording. To keep it, include a self-addressed envelope with enough postage or collect it at the office within 30 days, from the second business day after recording. The original carries no stamp and is not the official document. The county also publishes a list of companies that can electronically record real estate documents for Winnebago County.

sections.h2: How can you search Winnebago County land records?
sections.html:
You can search at public terminals in the Register of Deeds office, or online through paid access programs. Most records are available back to 1850, with indexes back to 1935. The office encourages appointments for morning sessions from 8:30 to 11:00 a.m. or afternoon sessions from 1:30 to 3:30 p.m., and walk-ins are served first come, first served with preference to those with appointments.

Tapestry is the online program for occasional users in real estate related work, and Laredo is for title firms and others who need daily access. Both charge fees for support and maintenance. A seller who wants to see the recorded mortgage, a prior deed or a recorded lien before listing a house can start at the terminals.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Winnebago County itself?
sections.html:
Winnebago County covers 579 square miles, of which 434 are land and 144, or 25 percent, are water. It was founded in 1848, takes its name from the Winnebago people, and had 171,730 residents in the 2020 census, with a 2025 estimate of 174,218. Oshkosh is the county seat and largest city, and the county makes up the Oshkosh-Neenah metropolitan area.

Cities in the county are Oshkosh, Neenah, Omro, Menasha and Appleton. Appleton is mostly in Outagamie and Calumet counties and Menasha is partly in Calumet County, so a parcel with an Appleton or Menasha address may sit in a different county than you expect. The county borders Waupaca, Outagamie, Calumet, Fond du Lac, Green Lake and Waushara counties.

Wittman Regional Airport serves the county, and Appleton International Airport in neighboring Outagamie County provides commercial airline service. Confirm the county first, because the deed is recorded in the county where the land lies.

faqs.q: How much does the Winnebago County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The charge is $30 per document, regardless of the number of pages. Copies of recorded documents are $2 for the first page and $1 for each added page, plus $1 if you want a certified copy.

faqs.q: Who pays the Wisconsin real estate transfer fee?
faqs.a: The seller pays it, as the grantor. The rate is 30 cents per $100 of value, which Winnebago County states as $3 per $1,000 rounded up to the next hundred, and the Register of Deeds collects it when the deed is submitted.

faqs.q: Do I need a transfer return to record a deed in Winnebago County?
faqs.a: Yes for most deeds. A return signed by both grantor and grantee, with the fee or an exemption number, is a condition of recording. The Department of Revenue now takes the return in My Tax Account, with no registration needed.

faqs.q: Can I get an official copy of my deed after recording?
faqs.a: Yes. Sign the SWIFT Agreement when you submit the document and the office sends a link, valid for 7 days, to print up to 3 copies. After that you pay the standard copy fee.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Winnebago County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Call 920-232-3390. The office is the county's repository for deeds, mortgages, land contracts, plats and vital records, and you can search records at its public terminals by appointment or first come, first served.
